study_identification_part.si_4_title: Adjustment of Regional Cortical Thickness Measures for Global Cortical Thickness Obscures Deficits Across the Schizophrenia Spectrum: A Cautionary Note About Normative Modeling of Brain Imaging Data

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Study 1: Single-site dataset from University of California San Francisco (UCSF) including HC, CHR-P, and ESZ participants. Study 2: Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis (HCP-EP) multi-site dataset from Indiana University, Brigham and Women's Hospital, and McLean Hospital including HC, NAff-P, and Aff-P participants.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Study 1 included healthy control participants (HCs), participants at CHR-P, and participants with early-illness schizophrenia (ESZ) who underwent MRI scanning at the University of California San Francisco."; "Study 2 included HCs, participants with nonaffective psychosis (NAff-P), and participants with affective psychosis (Aff-P) who underwent MRI scanning as part of the HCP-EP (Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis)."; "HC, non-affective psychosis (NAff-P), and affective psychosis (Aff-P) individuals were scanned at one of three sites (Indiana University [n=80], Brigham and Women's Hospital [n=46], and McLean Hospital [n=43]) as part of the Human Connectome Project-Early Psychosis (HCPEP) study."

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: This study is a methodological cautionary note examining the effect of global thickness adjustment on regional thickness profiles. It does NOT construct a normative model for application. Instead, it uses z-score normalization within each study: HC data are used to derive age, gender, (site), and (global thickness) regression parameters, which are then applied to compute deviation z-scores for all participants. The purpose is to demonstrate that adjusting for global thickness attenuates disease effects on regional thickness.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "ROI thicknesses were regressed on age, gender, and site (only study 2 included site) in HCs to model the effects of normal aging, gender, and site. Resulting parameter estimates were used to derive predicted ROI values for each participant, irrespective of group..."; "In this article, we focused on cortical thickness and the effect of global adjustment."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: This study performs within-study z-score normalization using only HC data from each study to derive regression parameters. No external validation or test sets are used for normative modeling. The HC samples are used entirely for deriving normalization parameters, not split into train/validation/test. Study 1: 90 HC from UCSF. Study 2: 56 HC from HCP-EP sites.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "Study 1 included 90 healthy control participants, 51 participants at clinical high risk for psychosis, and 78 participants with early-illness schizophrenia."; "Study 2 included 56 healthy control participants, 83 participants with nonaffective psychosis, and 30 participants with affective psychosis."; "HCs (n=90) did not meet DSM-IV Axis I criteria..."; "HCs (n=56) did not meet DSM-5 criteria for a mood or psychotic disorder..."
